paragraphs: Friend, here's what this song teaches me. The same LORD who restored the captives of Zion is the One the singers pray to when they say, "Restore our captives, O LORD, like streams in the Negev." (Psalm 126:1, 4) They remember what He did, and then they ask Him to do it again. Remembering what God has done is the fuel for asking Him for more.

Now look at the farm picture. "Those who sow in tears will reap with shouts of joy." (Psalm 126:5) The song never says the tears aren't real. The one who goes out weeping is carrying seed the whole time, and the song says he "will surely return with shouts of joy, carrying sheaves of grain." (Psalm 126:6) I think that's the comfort here: the weeping and the harvest both belong in the same story.

So baker, if you're in a season of tears right now, this song gives you a place to stand. You can be honest with the LORD about the sadness and still keep sowing. I've cried over a cold oven and a stack of dusty menus, and I'm telling you, I will take a song that holds both. Keep your seed in your hands, and keep singing.
